title: perf(core): parse files in parallel with bounded concurrency
problem: Parsing is single-threaded, so large repositories underutilize available cores.
why: Parsing dominates scan time; parallelism is the largest realistic speedup.
scope: Parse files concurrently with a bounded worker pool while preserving deterministic output.
Keep an opt-out for constrained environments.
guidance: Prefer a small internal thread pool over a heavyweight dependency if feasible; otherwise justify `rayon`.
security: Bound concurrency and memory to avoid resource exhaustion on huge repositories.
dod: Merged with benchmark numbers in the PR.

title: perf(bench): measure and report peak memory usage
problem: The benchmark reports throughput but not memory, yet memory matters for CI containers.
why: Prevents regressions that trade speed for unacceptable memory.
scope: Extend the benchmark example to sample and print peak RSS on supported platforms.
guidance: Use platform APIs with a graceful fallback when unavailable.
acceptance: Benchmark prints memory for each size
tests: Benchmark compiles and runs in CI build
deps: May add a small platform dependency.

title: perf(rules): add per-rule timing breakdown
problem: When scans are slow, it is unclear which rule dominates.
scope: Add an opt-in `--timings` flag reporting per-rule elapsed time to stderr.
guidance: Use `Instant` around each rule; keep output out of machine formats.

title: perf(ci): add a benchmark regression threshold
problem: Nothing detects a large performance regression before merge.
why: A loose threshold catches accidental quadratic behavior without flaky failures.
scope: Run the benchmark in CI and fail only when throughput drops beyond a generous factor vs. a recorded baseline.
guidance: Store the baseline in the repo; compare on the same runner type.
acceptance: CI job configured with a documented threshold
security: Avoid flakiness: use a wide margin and ubuntu-only.
